newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian police raid pirate CD manufacturer.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian police raid pirate CD manufacturer.

text.p: Bulgarian police seized equipment for producing pirated compact discs in a raid on the Unison factory in the town of Botevgrad on Thursday, the interior ministry said.

Bulgaria has promised to clamp down on the trade, in which it is thought to be second only to China. The International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI) says Bulgaria's annual production of 15 million pirated CDs costs the European recording industry $100 million a year.
The ministry statement said police had confiscated 5,070 pirate CDs, 44 master discs and the computer used for production.

"For the first time police seized five unlicensed master heads and three of them had no SID (identification) code," it said. Identification codes were introduced to mark legally produced discs and make pirate copies easier to identify.

A Reuters photographer who witnessed the raid on the Botevgrad plant some 40 km (25 miles) northeast of Sofia said police found boxes containing CDs without an identification code hidden in a storage area concealed in one of the walls of the building.
The IFPI has urged Bulgaria to act against five CD plants which are estimated to supply approximately one in eight of all illegal copies on the world black market.
The authorities face difficulties in fighting the trade which has blossomed since the end of one-party rule, taking advantage of Bulgaria's sophisticated technology and inadequate legal controls.
Bulgaria took its first case to the court this month but the defendant was acquitted for lack of evidence.
In the last six months police say they have investigated more than 280 producers and vendors of compact discs and confiscated hundreds of thousands of audio CDs.
In April police swooped on CD producers in Sofia and in the towns of Botevgrad, Veliko Tarnovo and Stara Zagora, inspecting production lines and stores and confiscating their illegal production.
